results.title: zCLOUD vs Paperspace: A Paperspace Alternative Compared on GPU Price, Regions and Billing
highlights:
October 20, 2026

Paperspace Machines are dedicated GPU virtual machines that DigitalOcean rents by the hour under the Paperspace name. zCLOUD is Zettabyte's GPU cloud, which pools NVIDIA H100 GPUs from 40+ providers and assigns the cheapest available at purchase.

zCLOUD costs less for the same GPU paid by the hour, starting at $3.75 per GPU per hour against Paperspace's $5.95. A three-year commitment cuts Paperspace's rate to $2.24, below zCLOUD's reserved rate from $2.79.

Paperspace charges a powered-off hourly machine for storage, which suits on-and-off development work.

...

Paperspace Machines bill the GPU by the hour while the machine runs. Storage and public IP addresses bill up to a monthly cap.

...

## Paperspace GPU Pricing Next to zCLOUD

Each pricing option suits a different kind of work, so compare the matching option on each side:

1. Paying by the hour: zCLOUD starts at $3.75 and Paperspace charges $5.95, which Paperspace labels a special promo price. Hourly pricing suits training runs and tests that last days or weeks.
2. Committing to a term: Paperspace drops to $2.24 on a three-year term, and zCLOUD's reserved rate starts at $2.79. A term pays off when your GPUs stay busy for most of its hours.
3. Interruptible capacity: neither pricing page lists a rate for capacity the provider can reclaim mid-job.

zCLOUD's published rates are starting prices, and zCLOUD confirms the exact rate when it assigns the GPUs.

...

Eight of these GPUs running 240 hours cost $11,424 on Paperspace Machines and from $7,200 on zCLOUD at hourly rates. The table assumes eight GPUs busy for each of the 240 hours.

...

1. Data transfer out: Paperspace's pricing docs say it doesn't charge machines for ingress or egress bandwidth, so copying datasets and checkpoints out stays off the Paperspace bill.
2. GPU model: zCLOUD sells H100 today and offers H200 and Blackwell through sales. A job tuned for a Paperspace A100, V100 or RTX A6000 needs a test run on zCLOUD's GPUs before you switch.
3. Stop-start habits: ask zCLOUD how it bills a stopped on-demand instance before you move on-and-off development work.

results.title: Paperspace GPU 怎么选？A6000、A100 80GB、H100 的小时价和关机规则 | 智机玄同
results.author: 智机玄同 发布于 2026年10月10日 2 分钟阅读
highlights:
# Paperspace GPU 怎么选？A6000、A100 80GB、H100 的小时价和关机规则

Paperspace Machines 当前公开 A6000、A100-80G、H100 等 GPU 小时价。本文解释整机配置、关机停 compute 与存储继续收费的区别。

智机玄同发布于 2026年10月10日 2 分钟阅读

资料核查日期： 2026年10月10日。价格、库存和服务商规则可能变化，请以官方页面为准。

文章目录

Paperspace 现在属于 DigitalOcean，但它的 Machines 计费逻辑和 DigitalOcean GPU Droplets 并不一样。

最重要的一条是：

Paperspace Machine 关机后，GPU compute 会停止计费。

不过存储、公网 IP 和其他附加资源仍可能继续收费。

## 当前几个高价值单卡价格

官方当前 GPU Machines 价格：

- RTX A6000 48GB：$1.89/小时
- A100-80G：$3.18/小时
- H100 80GB：$5.95/小时

Machine Types 文档还给出了整机配置。

RTX A6000：8 vCPU、45GB RAM；A100-80G：12 vCPU、90GB RAM；H100：20 vCPU、250GB RAM。

GPU Machines 默认 50GB SSD，可以扩容。

...

## Power Off 和 Destroy 有什么差别

Power Off：compute 停费，但机器还存在。

Destroy：如果附加资源也不再需要，才是彻底释放。

这点和 DigitalOcean GPU Droplet 的“关机仍收实例费”不同。

所以经常开开停停的用户，要把两种产品的生命周期规则分清楚。

...

H100 当前还可能需要容量审批，不能把公开价格理解成随时都有库存。

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Median on-demand prices for B300, B200, H200, H100, MI300X and more across specialist GPU clouds, converted to monthly cost, with how prices moved this year.

- November 4, 2026
- 7 min read
- By the CoreGPU team

Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

The lowest prices often come from marketplaces with variable host quality or from “starting at” prices that are rarely available. The median is a better picture of what a team actually pays for reliable capacity.

...

## Hyperscalers

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.

...

This index is updated monthly. Figures are public list prices observed on the date above and can change without notice.

results.title: Coinepay | How to Pay for Paperspace with a Virtual Card (Step-by-Step)
highlights:
## Understand Paperspace plans and pricing

Gradient lists Individual (“User”) and Team plans, each with Free, Pro and Growth tiers, plus an Enterprise contact-sales option. At the time of writing (November 2026), Individual Pro is listed at $0.0119/hour capped at $8/month and Growth at $0.0580/hour capped at $39/month; Team Pro is $0.0179/hour capped at $12/month and Growth $0.0580/hour capped at $39/month. These figures are published in USD; local-currency prices are not confirmed. Prices change, so always confirm the current amount on the official Paperspace pricing page before you subscribe.

Paperspace says payments are processed by Stripe and billed monthly on the first of the month. Paid machine usage is charged by machine type, and Gradient storage beyond your allowance is billed at $0.29/GB/month at the time of writing. Turning a machine off stops its compute charge, but attached storage, public IPs and other add-ons keep accruing until you destroy them — worth knowing so your card balance isn't drained by something you thought was switched off.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

Image: Verda via verda.com

What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 2, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.05 → $13.18 [$13.18], B300 $11.35 → $11.46 [$11.46], B200 $8.87 → $8.96 [$8.958], H200 $6.25 → $6.31 [$6.313], H100 SXM $4.79 → $4.84 [$4.841], A100 80GB $2.25 → $2.27 [$2.270], A100 40GB $1.61 → $1.63 [$1.625], RTX PRO 6000 $2.65 → $2.67 [$2.671] and L40S $1.90 → $1.92 [$1.920]. Each move is within a cent of +1.0% — a uniform list adjustment, not one card repricing.

...

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. ### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

results.title: Paperspace Alternatives (2026): 6 GPU Clouds Compared
results.author: OverGPU engineering
highlights:
Paperspace is now part of DigitalOcean, which points new users to its GPU Droplets. Six alternatives compared on billing, hardware and payment, then a fair look at dedicated monthly GPU servers.

...

If you are searching for a Paperspace alternative, you have probably noticed the change: Paperspace is now part of DigitalOcean, its core products still run, and new users are encouraged to sign up through DigitalOcean instead. It is a good moment to ask what your workload actually needs. If your GPUs run most of the month, a dedicated server at a flat monthly price can be simpler than usage billing. This page compares the options as of October 2026.

## Paperspace and DigitalOcean today

DigitalOcean folded the Paperspace brand into its own in 2024. According to DigitalOcean, core Paperspace products are still available, and new users are encouraged to sign up through DigitalOcean to access its GPU and AI products. For new GPU capacity, the main option there is GPU Droplets: virtual machines with one or eight GPUs, billed per second with a minimum billing period. DigitalOcean also offers 

12-month

 reserved contracts, spot plans and 

contract-only

 Bare Metal GPUs with eight GPUs per server.

...

| Criterion | OverGPU | Paperspace (DigitalOcean) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Billing model | Flat monthly price per server, billed in advance; per-GPU-hour equivalent published | Usage-based: GPU Droplets billed per second with a minimum billing period; Paperspace machines billed by usage |
| Minimum commitment | One month; cancel any month with no fee | None on demand; 12-month contracts for reserved GPU Droplets; Bare Metal GPUs by contract |
| Hardware tenancy | Whole physical GPUs for one customer: bare-metal 8-GPU servers or a dedicated VM with the full GPU passed through; no vGPU, MIG or time-sharing | GPU Droplets are VMs with 1 or 8 GPUs on shared physical hosts; Bare Metal GPUs are single-tenant 8-GPU servers under contract |
| GPU lineup focus | B300, B200, H200, H100, MI355X, RTX PRO 6000, L40S and RTX 5090; GB300 NVL72 on request | On demand: H100, H200, L40S, RTX 4000 Ada, RTX 6000 Ada and AMD MI300X; B300, MI325X and MI350X on contract; B300, MI350X and MI355X as spot plans |
| Data transfer and egress | 20 TB/month (single-GPU) or 50 TB/month (8-GPU) included, no egress fees, fair use; inbound not counted | GPU Droplets: outbound allowance per Droplet, then billed per GiB; inbound free. Paperspace Machines: no ingress or egress charges |
| Payment methods | Crypto (BTC, ETH, XMR, USDT TRC-20, SOL) via a prepaid USD balance, with a top-up bonus of up to 50%; card payments coming soon | Cards, PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, Alipay, Link, ACH for qualifying US customers, and crypto payments with limited availability |
| Support | 24/7 engineers; 99.9% monthly availability SLA with service credits | DigitalOcean: free 24/7 ticket support, with 24/7 chat on Standard and Premium plans. Paperspace: free ticket support seven days a week, Enterprise support by contract |
| Best for | Steady workloads that run most of the month: inference, long training and fine-tuning runs | Notebooks, experiments and teams already on DigitalOcean that want self-serve, usage-billed GPUs |

Paperspace and DigitalOcean details come from their public websites and documentation in October 2026 and can change, so check their current terms before you decide.

...

According to DigitalOcean, core Paperspace products are still available, and new users are encouraged to sign up through DigitalOcean for its GPU products. Check their current terms, as the lineup keeps changing.

results.title: Same GPU, up to 28× the price: the provider spread on 2026-10-10 - Obolith
highlights:
# Same GPU, up to 28× the price: the provider spread on 2026-10-10

One chip, every tracked provider, 1 GPU on-demand on 2026-10-10: the V100 spread is 28×, the B200 spread is 1.3×. Check the provider before the chip.

 Obolith · Last updated: 2026-10-12

Most GPU cost discussions start with the chip: H100 or A100, B200 or L40S. The data says the provider can matter just as much. Rent the same card as 1 GPU on-demand, and on 2026-10-10 the gap between the cheapest and most expensive tracked price ranged from 1.3× on the B200 to 28× on the V100.

This article reports those gaps. It does not explain them, and it compares nothing beyond the hourly rate. A marketplace listing and a provider's own instance are not necessarily the same product. That difference has its own section below.

## The spread table, 2026-10-10

For each chip: the cheapest and most expensive tracked price for 1 GPU on-demand, the multiplier between them, and how many providers we track for that card. Prices as of 2026-10-10.

| Chip (1 GPU, on-demand) | Cheapest | Most expensive | Spread | Providers tracked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V100 16GB | Vast.ai $0.082/h (marketplace) | Paperspace $2.30/h | 28× | 5 |
| A100 SXM 40GB | Vast.ai $0.362/h (marketplace) | Lambda $1.99/h | 5.5× | 6 |
| A10 22GB | Vast.ai $0.243/h (marketplace) | Lambda $1.29/h | 5.3× | 2 |
| RTX A4000 16GB | Hyperstack $0.15/h | Paperspace $0.76/h | 5.1× | 3 |
| RTX A5000 24GB | RunPod $0.27/h | Paperspace $1.38/h | 5.1× | 2 |
| RTX A6000 48GB | Hyperstack $0.50/h | Paperspace $1.89/h | 3.8× | 5 |
| L40S 45GB | Vast.ai $0.535/h (marketplace) | Verda $1.62/h | 3× | 3 |
| B200 192GB | Hyperstack $6.00/h | RunPod $7.99/h | 1.3× | 5 |

...

## B200 and L40S spreads

The B200 192GB sits at the other end: five providers within a 1.3× band, or 25% less from top to bottom. Same rule as above, bars start at zero on a common scale:

```text
B200 192GB, 1 GPU on-demand, 2026-10-10

Hyperstack             █████████████████████         $6.00/h
Vast.ai (marketplace)  ██████████████████████        $6.25/h
Lambda                 ███████████████████████▌      $6.69/h
Verda                  ██████████████████████████    $7.42/h
RunPod                 ████████████████████████████  $7.99/h

```

On the B200, the marketplace listing is not the cheapest; Hyperstack is. We report the observation only: this sample does not tell us why the B200 range is tight while the V100 range is wide, and we will not guess. At this price level, even a narrow spread is worth a look.

...

## What the hourly price doesn't tell you

The table compares one thing: the listed hourly price for 1 GPU, on-demand. It does not compare conditions of service, and those can differ.

Our data labels only the Vast.ai prices as marketplace listings. It does not classify the other offers, and we do not score any provider's service model here. The comparison is on price only.

Before you treat the cheapest row as a straight substitute, check these points on the provider's own terms:

- what availability and interruption terms apply to the listing;
- what the host, network and storage setup looks like, and what storage and egress cost on top;
- what support, uptime commitments and data handling you get;
- whether the exact configuration (memory, interconnect, region) matches what you need.

A wide spread is a signal to look closer, not a verdict on which offer is better value for your workload.

## Prices move too

The spread is a snapshot, and prices at a single provider can move meaningfully within a month. Verda's on-demand prices between 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-10:

| Chip | 2026-09-10 | 2026-10-10 | Change (30 days) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B200 SXM | $6.11/h | $7.42/h | +21% |
| H100 SXM | $3.25/h | $3.93/h | +21% |
| H200 SXM | $4.00/h | $5.12/h | +28% |
| V100 | $0.17/h | $0.206/h | +21% |

A B200 cost estimate built on the 2026-09-10 Verda price would already be out of date a month later. The same applies to any budget built from a one-time comparison.

## How to use it

1. Start from the chip page, not the provider page. Open the page for your card to see every tracked provider side by side: V100, A100, A10, RTX A4000, A5000, A6000, L40S, H100, H200, B200. Prices are collected daily, so check before each rental rather than relying on what you saw last time.
2. Shortlist by price, then filter by conditions. Take the cheapest few offers and go through the checklist above. Drop anything that fails your requirements.
3. Feed the real rate into your cost model. The hourly rate is one input. Idle hours, utilisation and the option of using an API decide the rest. Is it cheaper to self-host, or just use an API? and What does it really cost to run an LLM? walk through that arithmetic.
